name: Firstsource Solutions Ltd
tagline: RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group BPO/BFSI-Healthcare services firm growing via acquisitions and large deal wins, despite a recent profit-plunge quarter
business_overview: Firstsource Solutions, part of the RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group, provides business process management (BPO) services across Banking & Financial Services, Healthcare, and Communications/Media/Technology verticals.
fundamentals_table: Rs 341.9 Cr (up from zero in FY24)
fundamentals_narrative: Solid ROCE (16.8%) and ROE (17.6%) with revenue growth (19.67% CAGR) massively outpacing the industry median (3.91%). New long-term debt (Rs 341.9 Cr, up from zero) is explained by a string of recent acquisitions rather than distress, but a Q3 FY26 'profit plunge' headline alongside continued revenue growth suggests integration/investment costs are pressuring near-term margins.
technical_read: Trading around Rs 276, roughly mid-range within its Rs 201-382 52-week band.
sentiment_summary: Moderately active VP thread (43 replies, last activity 2026-06-23) with recent focus on the company's acquisition-led growth strategy.
community_signal: shyamutty (2026-06-23, 1 love) listed Firstsource's recent moves: a Rs 100 Cr investment in AppliedAI (Nov 2025), the TeleMedik acquisition (~$3M), the Pastdue Credit Solutions acquisition (£22M), four large deals signed with ACV over $5M each, and 17 large deals won in FY26 overall — also noting HDFC Small Cap fund has taken a large position in FSL, an institutional-interest signal.
bse_notes: Not checked this pass — the new long-term debt appears tied to disclosed acquisitions (AppliedAI, TeleMedik, Pastdue Credit Solutions) rather than an undisclosed red flag.
bull_case: 19.67% revenue CAGR vs. 3.91% industry median shows genuine market-share gains, not just organic drift
Active, disciplined M&A (AI capability via AppliedAI, healthcare via TeleMedik, BFSI collections via Pastdue) building out a broader services platform
17 large deals won in FY26 with several exceeding $5M ACV — real, quantified new business momentum
HDFC Small Cap fund holding a large position is a credible institutional-conviction signal
bear_case: Q3 FY26 'profit plunge' despite revenue growth signals real near-term margin/integration cost pressure from the acquisition spree
New leverage (Rs 341.9 Cr long-term debt, from zero) adds financial risk while integration is still underway
At Rs 19,514 Cr, already a well-covered mid-large-cap — a 10x/100x re-rating needs far more than steady BPO growth
BPO/BFS services margins are structurally thinner and more competitive than product/IP businesses
verdict_headline: Genuine acquisition-led growth story with institutional backing — but too large already and margin pressure needs to resolve
verdict_reasoning: Strong revenue growth and real deal-win momentum are positives, backed by a credible institutional holder (HDFC Small Cap)
But the profit plunge and new debt from acquisitions need to show a clear payoff before this looks re-rating-ready
Market cap size alone rules out a 10x/100x fit for this specific screen
